patch.value: A repeatable boolean extension switch mixed in attached and bare forms (--many=false --many) loses its bare occurrences, because Commander never sees the attached form

Found 2026-11-14 while fixing pm-gh1726 on the built CLI. A flag declared value_type boolean with repeatable: true is a switch (value_arity none), so Commander registers it without a value placeholder: a bare --many reaches the list accumulator, while --many=false is unknown to Commander and is read only by the loose parser from command.args. coerceAccumulatedLooseOption in src/sdk/extension/command-options.ts orders values from the loose occurrences whenever any exist, so the Commander-held bare values are dropped: pm <cmd> --many=false --many delivers [false] instead of [false, true], and --many --many=false delivers [false] instead of [true, false]. All-bare (--many --many, fixed in the same PR to [true, true]) and all-attached forms are unaffected. Fix direction: derive list-switch occurrences in argv order from the captured COMMAND_OPTION_TOKENS with the existing scanArgvScope grammar (refuseConflictingArgvOptionSpellings already resolves each spelling with Commander semantics), instead of mixing Commander's accumulator with the loose occurrence list. Duplicate check: searched repeatable boolean switch attached value order argv; pm-wlxf8f (closed) owns scalar spelling conflicts, pm-853a (closed) value-arity predicates; nothing owns list-switch occurrence order.

pm <cmd> --many=false --many delivers [false, true] and --many --many=false delivers [true, false] on the built CLI; Occurrence order for list switches comes from the same argv scanner that resolves spelling conflicts, so a token consumed as another option's value is never counted; An in-process spec drives mixed, bare-only and attached-only forms, with a negative control showing the pre-fix loss
Every occurrence of a repeatable switch reaches the handler in argv order
Bare occurrences are dropped when any attached occurrence is present

value.text: Narrowed 2026-11-14 by PR #1732: list flags no longer lose Commander-parsed values when an unrelated flag reaches the loose parser (readOrderedLooseListValues now falls back when no occurrence names the flag). What remains here is only the same-flag mix of attached and bare occurrences of a repeatable switch.
